decisions.reason: Having survived an initial portfolio shake-out and fitting the bakery's core rye range with low carrying cost, this bread still looks worth keeping as a modest but viable option despite limited differentiation.
As the firm's flagship seasonal stollen with a renewed gold medal and clear brand value, its quality and market appeal are already well revealed, giving management little reason to abandon it.

This variant remains inexpensive to offer within the core bread line, and after weaker bread experiments were already removed it is reasonable to keep it, though its niche profile still leaves some rationalization risk.

The marzipan stollen is a close-to-core seasonal extension that likely uses existing capabilities and adds assortment breadth at low incremental cost, so absent negative signals it should be kept for another season.
